title: Flames shoot from Kuromanta during an excavation in a thunderstorm

tellings.quote: They look back up and all of a sudden there's flames shooting out of the top of the mountain.

plain: During a dig on Kuromanta, a mountain in Akita, Japan, that some call a pyramid, workers caught in a thunderstorm are said to have looked up and seen flames shooting out of the top of the mountain. The researcher Geoffrey Drumm tells Michels this from a book by a man named Suzuki about the excavation, and gives no date. Drumm uses it to argue that pyramids were built to work as some kind of energy machine.
